title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Ops, and Top Issues (Playbook)
author: Priya Nair
body:
Overview

This playbook defines standards, templates, and operating procedures for all developer-experience (DevEx) documentation that supports the Redwood API, SDKs, and docs site. It covers: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, canonical API examples, docs-site operating procedures (publishing and rollbacks), and the canonical fixes for our top support issues. The goal is consistent, high-quality, discoverable docs that reduce time-to-success for engineers integrating Redwood inference.

Audience

- Developer experience engineers
- SDK owners
- Solutions and support engineers
- Technical writers

Scope

Applies to: user-facing SDK guides and quickstarts, API examples used in docs and SDKs, the docs site publishing process, and the canonical support-fix repository for recurring top issues. Not in scope: internal meeting notes and draft experiments (stored in Google Drive).

Standards and structure (required for every page)

Every DevEx document must include:

1. Title and short summary (1-2 sentences)
2. Scope and intended audience
3. Ownership (author, owner_team, reviewers)
4. Quickstart or TL;DR code snippet near the top
5. Step-by-step body with numbered procedures where applicable
6. Example requests and responses (curl, Python/JS snippets)
7. Troubleshooting / common errors section with canonical fixes
8. Related pages and labels
9. Last updated and changelog note

Templates and canonical artifacts

We maintain the following canonical templates in the quickstarts-and-templates directory:

- SDK Guide Template (sdk-guide-template.md) — sections and example snippets for Python, JavaScript, and Go.
- Quickstart Template (quickstart-template.md) — 5-10 minute setup and one working example.
- API Example Template (api-example-template.md) — request/response, edge cases, error handling.
- Code Snippet Style Guide (code-style.md) — import style, auth handling, and idiomatic examples.

Table 1: Quick reference for required fields in a quickstart

| Field | Required? | Example | Notes |
|------|----------|---------|-------|
| Title | yes | Embeddings quickstart | Short and searchable |
| TL;DR snippet | yes | Python + curl | Show minimal success path |
| Prereqs | yes | API key, pip install | Include versions |
| Step-by-step | yes | 1..N | Must be reproducible in 10 minutes |
| Troubleshooting | yes | common errors | Link to canonical fixes |

SDK guides: recommended layout

- Introduction and when to use this SDK
- Installation and supported versions (table of supported Python/Node/Go versions and package names)
- Auth patterns (env var, credential files, KMS patterns)
- Core objects and idioms (client, request/response, streaming)
- Examples: simple request, streaming response, function/tool calling, error handling
- Advanced: batching, caching, performance tips
- Migration notes between SDK versions

Example Python quickstart (TL;DR)

1) Install

pip install redwood-inference-sdk==1.4.0

2) Minimal example

from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
resp = client.text.generate(model='rw-instruct-1', prompt='Summarize the following: "Redwood is a developer-first inference platform"', max_tokens=60)
print(resp.text)

3) Curl example

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/text/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rw-instruct-1","prompt":"Hello world","max_tokens":32}'

API examples and canonical snippets

- All API examples must be published in three languages: curl, Python, and JavaScript (Node).
- Prefer concrete, copy-pasteable examples with realistic prompts and reasonable defaults.
- Include streaming and non-streaming variants where the feature is supported.

Canonical JavaScript example (excerpt)

import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const res = await client.text.generate({ model: 'rw-instruct-1', prompt: 'Translate to French: "Good morning"' })
console.log(res.text)

Docs site operating procedures (publishing, rollback, and maintenance)

Responsibilities

- DevEx on-call (rotation): perform reviews for publishing changes and handle build failures.
- Platform infra: maintain docs CI and hosting.
- Technical writers: content review for tone and completeness.

Publishing workflow (short)

1. Draft in the staging branch and create a pull request against docs-main.
2. Assign at least one devex reviewer and one SDK owner.
3. CI runs: markdown lint, code snippet execution tests, link-checker, and static search indexing tests.
4. After approvals and CI green, merge to docs-main. The merge triggers the staging build.
5. Run a smoke test suite (see checklist below). If green, promote staging to production during a low-traffic window (business hours PST preferred).

Docs smoke test checklist (must pass before promote)

- Load homepage and top-level product pages
- Execute 10 representative code snippets (curl, Python, Node)
- Verify redirects for any renamed pages
- Confirm search indexing for new labels and titles

Rollback procedure (if production regression discovered)

1. Open an incident in PagerDuty and tag docs-release.
2. Revert the docs-main merge commit and push.
3. Notify #devex and the release approvers with the revert PR link.
4. Once revert deploys, run the smoke tests.

Top support issues and canonical fixes (Q1-Q4 recurring list)

This section documents the top 8 support issues we see for SDKs and quickstarts along with the canonical remediation steps. Keep this short and include links to the relevant code examples and test suites.

Issue 1: Authentication failures (401)

- Symptom: curl or SDK returns 401 or "invalid_api_key".
- Canonical fix:
  1. Confirm REDWOOD_API_KEY is set in environment: echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY
  2. Check key has not expired in the customer portal
  3. Verify header is set correctly: Authorization: Bearer <key>
  4. Run curl -v to inspect request and server response

Issue 2: Streaming output stalls or disconnects

- Symptom: long-running streaming requests hang mid-response.
- Canonical fix:
  1. Confirm client uses keep-alive and correct chunked transfer encoding.
  2. For Node clients, ensure event loop is not blocked by synchronous work.
  3. If using proxies or corporate gateways, whitelist stream endpoints and test direct connection.

Issue 3: Model selection causing high latency

- Symptom: Unexpected high latency for small requests.
- Canonical fix:
  1. Check model variant and sequence length config. Prefer low-latency variant (e.g., rw-instruct-1-small) for interactive routes.
  2. Review batching configuration: some endpoints default to batch window = 50ms, adjust in SDK calls if low-latency required.

Issue 4: Mismatched schema errors on structured outputs

- Symptom: SDK raises validation errors or parsing fails.
- Canonical fix:
  1. Confirm the model is invoked with structured_output true and include a JSON schema example in the request.
  2. Add a small validation harness in the quickstart to show expected schema and keys.

Issue 5: Package installation/version mismatches

- Symptom: Import errors or API surface differs from docs.
- Canonical fix:
  1. Verify package version with pip show / npm list.
  2. Update the quickstart top-of-file to pin the validated SDK version.
  3. If breaking change, add a migration note to the SDK guide.

Issue 6: Rate limiting and 429 handling

- Symptom: Clients receive 429 when traffic bursts occur.
- Canonical fix:
  1. Implement exponential backoff with capped retries (recommended default: 3 retries, initial backoff 200ms, factor 2).
  2. Surface X-RateLimit-Remaining headers to the caller.

Issue 7: Embedding mismatches (dimension errors)

- Symptom: Downstream stores expect 1536-d vectors but client sends 1024-d.
- Canonical fix:
  1. Verify model embedding dimension in the API example (model: rw-embed-1536)
  2. Add quickstart snippet demonstrating vector shape check using numpy.length

Issue 8: Docs search not finding new quickstarts

- Symptom: Published quickstart not visible in search for 24+ hours.
- Canonical fix:
  1. Verify the docs change included labels and title.
  2. Re-run the search-index job: 
     - CI job: docs/indexer:latest run-index --pages <new-page-id>
     - If job fails, check indexer logs in CloudWatch under /docs/indexer.

Canonical fixes must be kept minimal and executable. If a fix requires infra changes, open an infra ticket and mark the issue as "requires-infra" in the tracker.

Ownership, metrics, and SLAs

- Owner: DevEx team (rotating on-call).
- Key metrics to track: snippet-execution success rate, search indexing latency, docs build success rate, time-to-merge for quickstart PRs.
- Targets: snippet execution >= 98%, docs build success >= 99%, indexing latency < 1 hour for 95% of pages.

Changelog and review cadence

- Quarterly content review: every SDK guide and quickstart must be reviewed at least once per quarter by the SDK owner.
- Minor clarifications: documented as in-line edits and a one-line changelog entry at the top of the page.

Appendix A — Example table of SDK installation versions

| SDK | Package | Recommended version | Notes |
|-----|---------|---------------------|-------|
| Python | redwood-inference | 1.4.0 | LTS for 2026 Q1 |
| Node | @redwood/inference | 1.4.0 | Node 18+ supported |
| Go | github.com/redwood/inference | v0.9.2 | Example client API stable |

Appendix B — Useful CLI and CI commands

- Run snippet execution tests locally: make docs-snippet-test
- Lint markdown: npx markdownlint-cli docs/**/*.md
- Re-index a single page: docs/indexer run-index --page-id <page-id>

Contact and escalation

- Primary on-call: devex-oncall rotation (see rota in team wiki)
- Slack channels: #devex, #docs-release, #platform-ci
- PagerDuty: devex-oncall escalation policy (for production docs regressions)

Notes

This playbook is the canonical single-source for DevEx docs standards. If you need a new template or change the publishing policy, open a PR against this page and tag the reviewers listed in the metadata.
